text: Write an interface with a `default` method and a class that never mentions it. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static class Dot implements Drawable { public String name() { return "dot"; } }
answer: default String label() { return "shape: " + name(); }|String name()|new Dot().label()
explanation: Verified: `shape: dot`. `Dot` never mentions `label` and has it anyway, which is exactly what let Java 8 add `sort`, `forEach` and `removeIf` to `List` without breaking implementations the JDK authors had never seen. Note that a default method may call the abstract ones, so it can supply real behaviour built out of the contract rather than merely a stub.
